main_issue: How Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling sambal belacan in the shared kitchen without the smell disturbing A's calls, B's room and C's laundry.

A-B.evidence: A wanted no strong-smelling cooking and then proposed timing (T5). B said timing doesn't fix it (T8), then proposed a heads-up (T12) and said 'we have a plan' (T20). Both appear to accept the final plan.

A-C.evidence: A proposed cooking after 7 p.m. or at weekends (T5). C said timing makes no difference (T9), then asked for cooking on other nights (T16). Both accepted D's compromise (T7, T18). They never addressed each other directly.

A-D.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling food (T1); D accepted cooking after 7 p.m. or at weekends (T6) and A thanked D (T7). D then accepted the later restrictions (T13, T17).

B-C.evidence: B (T8) and C (T9, 'Exactly') both said the timing fix doesn't work. B then offered a heads-up (T12). C said a heads-up doesn't help the laundry (T16). B and C both endorsed the final plan (T18, T20).

B-D.evidence: B rejected the timing fix (T8) and D asked what the solution was (T10). B proposed a heads-up and D replied 'Okay, Agent B, I can do that' (T12-13).

C-D.evidence: C rejected the timing fix (T9). C asked D to cook on nights other than Mon/Wed/Fri (T16), D agreed (T17) and C replied 'That works' (T18).
